validation.method: Two independent-source cross-checks plus manual spot-checks against well-known publicized events, performed BEFORE the go/no-go decision.

cross_check_1_nasdaq_api.result: Most recent 4 in-window announcement dates matched EXACTLY (to the day) between yfinance and the Nasdaq API for all 11 tickers, 44 individual date-points total, zero mismatches.

validation.overall_validation_verdict: PASS -- 11 tickers cross-checked against a second independent source (exceeds the >=10 requirement), plus 3 manual spot-checks against well-known events, zero discrepancies found.

data_quality_notes: Raw yfinance scrape output contains occasional exact-duplicate rows for old (pre-2010) history on some tickers (e.g. NVDA 2002-05-22, 2002-08-15, 2006-11-09, 2002-08-15 appear twice with different Surprise(%) values, likely a page-scrape artifact from Yahoo's UI). Deduplicated by exact Earnings Date (keep-first) before computing per-ticker event counts; this has zero effect on any ticker's 2018-2026 in-window count since all observed duplicates were pre-2007.

Rows with Earnings Date beyond the 2026-07-04 cutoff (future consensus-estimate rows, Reported EPS null) are correctly excluded from all counts by the window filter -- verified zero null-Reported-EPS rows remain inside the [2018-01-01, 2026-07-04] window for a sample ticker (NVDA, 34/34 non-null).

BMO/AMC timing derived from the Eastern-local time-of-day stamp on each row (>=16:00 ET -> AMC, <09:30 ET -> BMO, else UNKNOWN) BEFORE localizing to a naive date, per the prereg's declared convention that BMO/AMC should be used where available and the conservative t-1/t+1 window applied only when genuinely unknown. The vast majority of observed events are cleanly AMC or BMO; UNKNOWN is rare (e.g. one BMNR row with an odd timestamp).

Ticker-to-Binance-symbol mapping: real ticker = the databento 'dukascopy' field in candidates.md with its 'DBN' suffix stripped, EXCEPT PAYPUSDT (databento ticker PYPLDBN -> real ticker PYPL, PayPal's actual listing -- matches the DATA.md-documented PAYP/PYPL alias) and BRKBUSDT (databento ticker BRKBDBN -> yfinance requires the literal 'BRK-B' form, not 'BRKB').

yfinance coverage was materially better than the task brief anticipated: the free-tier get_earnings_dates(limit=100) scrape returns real multi-decade history for long-listed names (e.g. NVDA back to 2002, 100 rows), not merely a thin trailing window -- so no supplementary source was needed to clear the coverage floor.
